messages:
Sam: Quick thought — we've been seeing a lot of routing flaps when client retries beat the server fallback. Proposing a small client-side debounce/retry-backoff window in the SDKs (opt-in initially). 50-200ms range. reduces route churn and noisy telemetry. anyone opposed?
Jordan: +1 for reducing noise. curious about UX though — opt-in vs opt-out? and how this shows up in Console metrics (latency buckets, failed requests). :thinking_face:
Neha: Agree on the concept. My worry: adding debounce changes apparent latency from the user's perspective and might mask real infra issues. We should expose the raw timings in telemetry and a flag in Console so SREs can opt to see pre-debounce vs post-debounce numbers.
Max: From SDK side this is small: add `client.retry_debounce_ms` config, default 0 (off). Example patch:```json
{"client": {"retry_debounce_ms": 100, "max_retries": 2}}
```We can gate default to Dedicated customers later.
Sam: Good call on default-off. We should also tie this to quota accounting: do we charge for the extra attempted token usage before debounce? ideally debounce prevents extra requests entirely, so quota shouldn't be affected. Need product sign-off.
Jordan: Console changes: add a toggle in the per-customer settings: "Show pre-debounce events" and a new chart for "Client-debounce induced delay". Also surface the SDK version that enabled debounce in per-route traces.
Neha: Telemetry details: we should add a header `x-rw-client-debounce-ms` so backend can log it and we can slice traces. Sampling: include it in trace payload for 1% of requests by default. Careful with PII and sampling docs.
Max: Implementation plan for SDKs: Python/TS/Go all accept same config key. TS and Go can ship in minor releases; Python might need a major bump because of import changes we want. Will open PRs.
Sam: Rollout UX: recommend opt-in via SDK param for first 2 weeks, then flip to opt-out for beta accounts with heavy bursts. We'll announce in release notes and add a Console banner.
Jordan: Product question: if debounce > 0 and a request ultimately fails, do we surface it differently in the dashboard (debit vs retry-failure)? I think we should mark failures that occurred after debounce as "suppressed-retry" to help debugging.
Neha: +1 to "suppressed-retry" tag. Also add a link to raw logs from the Console trace to see exact sequence: request -> debounce -> retry -> backend response.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: routing-service v2.14.1 -> canary at 1717001200. Note: logging schema change incoming to accept `x-rw-client-debounce-ms` header.
Max: I'll coordinate PRs for TS/Go today. Sam — want me to add a short e2e test that ensures no duplicate route hinting occurs when debounce is non-zero?
Sam: Yes please. Also add a tiny perf test for 0/50/200ms to show impact on observed route churn. Put results in the Console rollout tile.
Jordan: I'll stub the Console tile and the admin toggle. Neha — can you draft the telemetry schema and sampling plan?
Neha: On it, will ping in #eng-platform when draft ready.
Sam: Cool. Action items: Max -> SDK PRs & e2e; Jordan -> Console tile & toggle; Neha -> telemetry schema; Sam -> product note + rollout plan. We'll reconvene after PRs. :thumbsup:
